name: Can radiant floor heating be installed underneath bathroom tile?

mainEntity.name: Can radiant floor heating be installed underneath bathroom tile?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, radiant floor heating systems must be laid directly onto the prepared subfloor before the tile is set in mortar. Electric heating mats or cables are secured, embedded in self-leveling underlayment or thin-set, and wired to a wall-mounted thermostat. Adding heating slightly raises the floor elevation, which requires careful planning around baseboards, door clearance, and toilet flanges. Once embedded, porcelain and ceramic tiles conduct and retain the warmth efficiently.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, radiant heating cables or mats can be installed over the subfloor and embedded in thin-set mortar right before the tile is laid.
